fixes.explanation: That's it, baker. The centurion, an army officer, hears about Jesus and sends Jewish elders to ask Him to come and heal his servant (Luke 7:3). His servant is sick and about to die. I think when somebody you care about is that sick, you go to the One who can help.

Nice thought, friend, but nobody's asking for a house blessing here. The elders carry a request "…to ask Him to come and heal his servant." (Luke 7:3). The servant is about to die, so healing is what this ask is about.

I get why you'd guess that, baker, since he's an officer with soldiers. But the elders aren't carrying a message about training anybody. The text says he sent them "…to ask Him to come and heal his servant." (Luke 7:3). His servant is sick and about to die, so healing is the request.

You got it, baker. The elders say, "…he loves our nation and has built our synagogue." (Luke 7:5) Love for the people and a building to show for it. That's a reason you can point at, and the elders plead earnestly with Jesus about it (Luke 7:4).

Good things, friend, but those aren't the reasons the elders give. They say the centurion "…loves our nation and has built our synagogue." (Luke 7:5) Feeding the poor and keeping the Sabbath never come up in their words. The synagogue is the thing he built.

Good guess, baker, but fasting and giving to the temple aren't what the elders say. They say the centurion "…loves our nation and has built our synagogue." (Luke 7:5) A synagogue is what he built, and that's what they bring up.

Not quite, friend. The centurion's message says, "Lord, do not trouble Yourself, for I am not worthy to have You come under my roof." (Luke 7:6) Nothing in it tells Jesus to hurry inside. He tells Jesus not to trouble Himself.

Right, baker. The centurion's message says, "Lord, do not trouble Yourself, for I am not worthy to have You come under my roof." (Luke 7:6) There's no "hurry inside" anywhere in it. He calls Jesus "Lord" and says he's not worthy to have Him come under his roof.

You got it, baker. The text says, "When Jesus heard this, He marveled at the centurion." (Luke 7:9) Jesus heard those words about authority and was amazed. Then He turns to the crowd and says, "I tell you, not even in Israel have I found such great faith." (Luke 7:9)

Close in sound, baker, but there's no sigh in the text. It says Jesus "…marveled at the centurion." (Luke 7:9) He was amazed by what the man said. Then He turns to the crowd and says, "I tell you, not even in Israel have I found such great faith." (Luke 7:9)
